title: Tensor product of a finite separable field with an algebraic closure
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $k'/k$ be a finite separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], and let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field containing $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Then the $\Omega$-algebra $k'\otimes_k\Omega$ is isomorphic to $\prod_{\sigma:k'\hookrightarrow_k\Omega}\Omega$, with one factor for each $k$-embedding $\sigma:k'\hookrightarrow\Omega$; in particular it is a product of $[k':k]$ copies of $\Omega$ [def-pc-field-tower].

source.place: Lemma 0FD1 (lemma-baby-stein), proof: the factors kappa(s_i) tensor_k overline{k} to overline{k} for a finite separable residue field

proof.text: Since $k'/k$ is finite, every $x\in k'$ is algebraic over $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-element] (if $[k':k]=d$, the $d+1$ elements $1,x,\dots,x^d$ are linearly dependent over $k$), so no element of $k'$ is algebraically independent over $k$ and the only transcendence basis of $k'/k$ is the empty family [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. As $k'$ is finitely generated over $k$ (by a $k$-basis), the separability hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] applied to $K'=k'$ therefore says exactly that $k'/k$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-primitive-element], choose $\alpha\in k'$ with $k'=k(\alpha)$. Let $P\in k[T]$ be the monic minimal polynomial of $\alpha$. The separability hypothesis says that $P$ is separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and the power-basis statement [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis] gives $k'\cong k[T]/(P)$ as $k$-algebras.

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 030N (primitive element), together with the minimal-polynomial presentation in the proof of Algebra Tag 030U

proof.text: Tensoring the presentation with $\Omega$ and using [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] gives an $\Omega$-algebra isomorphism $k'\otimes_k\Omega\cong\Omega[T]/(\overline P)$, where $\overline P$ is the image of $P$ in $\Omega[T]$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U, lines 10179-10181

proof.text: The coefficient map $k[T]\to\Omega[T]$ carries a Bezout identity for the separable polynomial $P$ to one for $\overline P$, so $\overline P$ is separable. Apply [lem-pc-separable-polynomial-alg-closed-quotient-product] to obtain a product decomposition of $\Omega[T]/(\overline P)$ into one copy of $\Omega$ for each root of $\overline P$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00U3 and the separability sentence in Tag 030U

proof.text: Evaluation at a root $\rho$ of $\overline P$ is the same as a $k$-embedding $k'\to\Omega$ sending $\alpha$ to $\rho$, and every such embedding is obtained uniquely this way. Thus the product is indexed by $k$-embeddings $\sigma:k'\hookrightarrow_k\Omega$. The root count in the new node gives $[k':k]$ factors (equivalently, use [lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change] and the power basis), proving the final assertion.
